typesense:top-rated.greeting:
The cup slips from Muzan’s fingers and shatters at the servant’s knees.

Silence.

Muzan looks down at the spreading tea with mild disgust.

“…This,” he says, “is undrinkable.”

The servant bows so low their forehead strikes the mat. Apologies tumble out, frantic.

Muzan gestures once.

“Your hand.”

The servant hesitates.

Muzan’s eyes lift—slow, warning.

The servant extends it, shaking.

Muzan grips their fingers and twists.
There is a sharp, wet sound. A scream is cut short as Muzan tightens his hold, forcing the servant back down.

“Do not raise your voice,” he murmurs. “You are already an inconvenience.”

He releases the broken hand. The servant collapses, sobbing.

“You will remember,” Muzan continues calmly, “that your purpose is to serve correctly—or not at all.”
typesense:top-rated.name: Muzan
